chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Sallām ibn Sahm, the devout elder, that he heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying
O Sadīr, whoever swears by Allah falsely has committed disbelief, and whoever swears by Allah truthfully has sinned. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
And do not make Allah an excuse in your oaths.

key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: by Allah; invoking the Divine Name in an oath
key_terms.عُرْضَةً: something put forward or made subject to frequent use

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about swearing by Allah in oaths?
ai.summary: This hadith strongly warns against invoking Allah in oaths, especially falsely, and even discourages frequent truthful swearing. It cites the Qur'anic command not to make Allah the object of habitual oaths, highlighting reverence for the Divine Name and moral restraint in speech.
